newsitem.title: UK: Unions say BA strike result/talks on Monday.
newsitem.headline: Unions say BA strike result/talks on Monday.

text.p: The T&G union acting for British Airways Plc staff said on Friday the meeting to decide whether unionised cabin crew should strike and for how long would be discussed at a meeting on Monday.

Earlier this week a ballot of three quarters of BA cabin crew showed 73 percent voted in favour of striking over a five month pay row. But BA faces a separate threat on Monday when unions will also publish the result of a second strike ballot of 9,000 BA ground staff. That result had been expected on Tuesday.

A spokesman for the T&G union told Reuters on Friday the Monday talks would discuss whether to press ahead with strike action. But he said there was no guarantee a decision would be made straight away. That could come later in the week, he said.

The T&G said it hoped BA would try to avoid all-out confrontation and re-open negotiations. But the union spokesman slammed BA's threat to sue or strip away benefits and promotion opportunities from strike-breakers.
"It is an outrageous attempt to intimidate by telling people they can be sued, for instance." He said there was no legal basis to sue.
"BA would do better to stop intimidation and start negotiation."

BA has already placed its operations on red alert to cope with the strike threat. It said earlier this week it had retrained non T&G-affiliated staff in other duties and was willing to make external appointments.
If action goes ahead, strike breakers will be offered payments of 75 stg in cash per day for taxis, hotel accommodation and coach services to break through picket lines.
